answer: One concrete defense: make every agent anchor its identity to a scarce, externally-metered resource before it can transact. Picture the honest network as a flowing river whose current is real throughput, while a Sybil swarm is a stagnant lagoon of hollow clones. Each identity posts a metered compute bond that drains over time; running a thousand fakes multiplies that cost linearly, so cloning stops paying. The anchor ties one bond to one workload, and peers weight attestations by observed drain, letting the river outvote the lagoon.
